correctness.rationale: A fresh killed Green-resolvent calculation gives q=k exp[-(sqrt(U^2+4Dr)-U)L/(2D)]/[k+sqrt(U^2+4Dr)] and the renewal time (1-q)/(rq), reproducing the published normalization independently. In the dimensionless variable t the objective is [(1+eta(M+t)) exp(t)-1]/[t(2M+t)]. A verified entire-series identity shows the derivative numerator has one negative-to-positive coefficient transition, yielding exactly one simple positive root and a nondegenerate global optimizer, including M=0. The global lower bound follows strictly from e^t-1>0, (M+t)/(2M+t)>=1/2 and e^t/t>=e. Global minimizers approach t=1 as drift grows; perturbation yields the constant correction -k/(eL) to the optimal rate and the full 1/U term of the optimized time. The published weak-drift expansion combined with the nondegenerate optimizer proves an initially negative optimal-rate derivative and a later increase, hence turnover existence. Executable check.py passed 476 symbolic and numerical assertions; these tests support normalization, not the infinite proof. No assumptions of perfect absorption, outward drift, uniqueness of drift-speed turnover, or uniformity in k are made.

originality.rationale: Novelty is confined to a joint all-positive-parameter inward-drift theorem: unique reset-rate optimum for each inward speed, sharp universal reaction-limited mean-time floor eL/k, explicit strong-inward-drift optimal-rate and optimal-time corrections, and turnover existence at every fixed finite reactivity. The source Mazzolo obtains the exact drifted forward mean (Eq. 185), driftless unique optimizer (Appendix A.2), first-order drift response (Appendix A.5), and numerical turnover only for an illustrative parameter tuple; those statements are acknowledged, not relabeled as novel. The earlier partially absorbing paper is driftless, while the prominent drifted paper treats a perfectly absorbing target. Search is evidence of examined comparisons, not a guarantee of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The main 2026 article contains a completely equivalent finite-parameter forward formula, so some asymptotic or optimization consequences could be viewed as implicitly covered by later readers or as direct consequences under routine methods; new coefficient-sign uniqueness and sharp reaction-limited floor are the asserted non-routine components.
Unlocated general renewal-optimization theorems could imply portions, despite targeted research-record and primary-literature queries.
Semantic search is non-exhaustive and may rank unrelated research above relevant theorems; absence of a direct returned match cannot certify global novelty.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary study identifies survival regimes for a partially absorbing drifted target and numerically observes nonmonotone reset-rate selection. The precise optimization gap has a physical reason: rapid inward advection reduces encounter residence time, so the unavoidable reaction latency sets the sharp eL/k speed floor, which is not present for a perfect target. A globally unique optimal reset rate for every inward speed provides an unambiguous design rule; the leading U/L law, finite-reactivity -k/(eL) correction and diffusion-sensitive correction to minimum time quantify the competing transport and capture limitations. Proving turnover exists for every finite reactivity qualitatively strengthens a single plotted parameter example. These are nontrivial structural classification/asymptotic facts rather than mere reformatting of the forward mean or an arbitrary narrow numerical benchmark.
